entities.summary: Lucius Apronius Caesianus was a Roman procurator and administrator in the Roman province of Dacia during the reign of Emperor Trajan (98-117 CE), a period marked by significant military conquests, economic growth, and cultural achievements. As a key figure in the administration of Dacia, he played a crucial role in overseeing the province's governance, taxation, and infrastructure development. His tenure also coincided with the reign of Emperor Hadrian (117-138 CE), who implemented significant reforms in the Roman Empire, including the creation of a new provincial administration and the expansion of Roman citizenship. Despite the scarcity of direct information on his personal life, Caesianus' legacy can be seen in the enduring impact of Roman rule on Dacia and the surrounding regions. The inscription on his tombstone, which has been recovered and partially deciphered, testifies to his administrative prowess and provides valuable insights into the governance of Dacia during this period. The archaeological record of the Dacian cities he oversaw, such as Ulpia Traiana Sarmizegetusa, reveals the sophisticated urban planning and engineering skills of the Roman administrators under his supervision. Moreover, the extensive network of roads, bridges, and public buildings he oversaw continues to shape the landscape of modern-day Romania and neighboring countries. Through his contributions to the administration of Dacia, Lucius Apronius Caesianus played a significant role in shaping the Roman Empire's expansion and legacy in the region.
